params.body:
Autobedrijf Gielkens meldt sinds 17 september dat een prijswijziging afketst met "This page has expired". The explanation we had (the session expiring) was refuted on 21 September: `SESSION_LIFETIME` is 43,200 minutes on production, thirty days. Four conversations long, five explanations stayed equally likely, because a 419 left no trace at all: it is deliberately not mailed (`doWeWantAMail` excludes `TokenMismatchException`) and the page catches it.

So `report()` now writes one line: who it happened to, on which screen, which Livewire method was called, whether a delegation was active, and how many input fields arrived next to what PHP accepts. That last pair is the point. PHP truncates a POST above `max_input_vars` (1000 here) without a word and drops the rest, the CSRF field included: same message, different cause. Reads 1000 of 1000 and the cause is found, and it is not about sessions.

Nothing changes for the visitor. The next time it happens it is a measurement instead of a guess.

Fixes bevinding een-419-liet-geen-spoor-na
params.title: A page that expires says who it happened to
